name: Cursor
scope: Cursor desktop Agent and Plan Mode in an existing repository; terminal/browser verification enabled, plan-dependent usage.
summary: A codebase becomes a controllable place to propose, implement and inspect software changes.
limitation: Diffs and tests verify chosen properties; they do not guarantee correct requirements or visual fidelity.

centerEvidence.claim: An existing-code feature or fix puts the default toward faithful, controlled implementation.

sources.title: Cursor Agent overview
sources.finding: Code search, file edits, terminal execution, browser verification and checkpoints support iterative repository work.

sources.title: Cursor Plan Mode
sources.finding: Researches code, clarifies requirements, and produces editable plans for multi-approach architectural work.

sources.title: Cursor Agent Review
sources.finding: Dedicated review examines local code changes.

N.claim: File and terminal operations can be specified and checked through commands and browser verification.

NE.claim: Bounded repository changes combine inspectable files with verification and rollback checkpoints.

E.claim: Exact file contents and deterministic terminal operations make scoped preservation independently checkable.

SE.claim: Architecture planning uses the current repository and user-edited constraints.

S.claim: Editable architecture plans explore requirements and multiple implementation approaches.

SW.claim: Planning an unfamiliar feature develops new software structure before implementation.

W.claim: New code and project assets allow substantial composition beyond templates.

NW.claim: A specified feature is authored across files and checked in the running application.

adjustments.reason: Tighten the existing-code proposal corner; proposal breadth is not preservation of all behavior.

name: Claude Code
scope: Coding agent with repository files, command execution, diffs and tests; suitable paid account or API access.
summary: Broad software invention, with a strong upper-right reach for specified edits checked against code and tests.
limitation: Tests verify selected properties, not every requirement; no automatic CAD or pixel-preservation claim.

centerEvidence.claim: A scoped repository change with tests is the illustrative default.

sources.title: Claude Code overview
sources.finding: Reads and edits repositories, executes commands, exposes diffs and integrates tools.

sources.title: Claude Code common workflows
sources.finding: Describes planning, alternative fixes, refactoring with behavior preserved, and running tests.

N.claim: Specified file operations can be executed and verified through diffs and tests.

NE.claim: Refactoring combines bounded edits with tests of retained behavior; coverage limits the joint reach.

E.claim: Deterministic file operations and unchanged-file diffs make exact scoped preservation checkable.

SE.claim: Alternative fixes can be considered within an existing codebase, without guaranteed equivalence.

S.claim: Plans and alternative fixes support originating software approaches under constraints.

SW.claim: Planning new features combines substantive invention with approach selection.

W.claim: Creates new features across multiple files, beyond fixed templates.

NW.claim: A specified feature can be authored and tested, while implementation retains discretion.

name: Lovable
scope: Lovable web Chat, Plan and Build modes for hosted web apps; preview selection, diffs and requested verification. Usage credits apply.
summary: Conversation develops app directions, then turns selected decisions into visible code changes.
limitation: Verification tools often require an explicit request; generated app behavior still needs acceptance checks.

centerEvidence.claim: The representative task is a conversational new app build with iterative feedback.

sources.title: Lovable Build mode
sources.finding: Implements across files, exposes diffs, permits file constraints, and can run browser, frontend and backend verification.

sources.title: Lovable Plan mode
sources.finding: Compares approaches and tradeoffs, develops architecture, and edits a reviewable plan before building.

sources.title: Lovable preview toolbar
sources.finding: Select and annotate elements to direct preview-based changes.

N.claim: File-addressed instructions, diffs and requested tests make constrained implementation inspectable.

NE.claim: Named-file boundaries and tests support controlled refactoring, without a universal preservation promise.

E.claim: Existing components, file constraints and diffs support strong structural retention.

SE.claim: Plans inspect existing code and identify affected components before revising an approach.

S.claim: Tradeoff comparisons and editable architecture plans support developed alternatives.

SW.claim: Plan mode compares new app architectures and develops a selected direction.

W.claim: Coordinated frontend, backend and generated asset changes provide broad app composition.

NW.claim: An approved implementation plan leads to multi-file construction with visible checks.

adjustments.reason: Emphasize conversational new-app planning relative to file-first coding agents.

name: Emergent
scope: Emergent full-stack app sessions with Build/Plan and live preview; excludes E3 and Brainstorm Plan-mode availability and Pro-only Maxx.
summary: An app idea quickly becomes a proposed structure and a running preview you can revise.
limitation: Preview checks and checkpoints are limited; rollback does not restore database records or validate the whole app.

centerEvidence.claim: A new app described in conversation delegates substantial structure choices before review.

sources.title: Emergent build and preview
sources.finding: Builds from descriptions, performs automatic error checks, and supports prompt-driven iteration in a live preview.

sources.title: Emergent discussion and planning
sources.finding: Discusses app types and approaches, then presents an adjustable plan before code generation.

sources.title: Emergent checkpoints
sources.finding: Supports code rollback and independent forks; database data is not restored by rollback.

N.claim: Specific feedback directs inspectable preview changes, with automatic error checks.

NE.claim: A targeted change can be exercised in preview; prompt compliance is not exact preservation.

E.claim: Code checkpoints and forks retain states, while database records sit outside rollback.

SE.claim: Plans retain app context while proposing revised structure and integrations.

S.claim: Discussion compares app approaches and revises a proposed build plan.

SW.claim: Exploring app types and architecture develops new directions before construction.

W.claim: App descriptions become code, structure and functioning interfaces.

NW.claim: A specified app feature can be generated and exercised, with implementation discretion.

adjustments.reason: Accent the distinction between inspectable previews and stronger file-level preservation controls.

name: Bolt
scope: Bolt browser app builder with Plan Mode, code targeting/locks and visual edits; free/paid token limits vary.
summary: A browser prototype can open into alternatives or narrow to selected files and components.
limitation: File locks bound edits; generated behavior and database changes require separate checks.

centerEvidence.claim: A chosen prototype feature is built in the browser with targeted edits and visible code.

sources.title: Bolt Code view
sources.finding: Target files, lock files/directories and reference selected code to constrain AI edits.

sources.title: Bolt Plan mode guide
sources.finding: Reads existing projects, suggests design changes, compares services and creates revisable plans before building.

sources.title: Bolt visual edits
sources.finding: Preview-based editing provides a way to address particular interface elements.

sources.title: Bolt overview
sources.finding: Builds websites and apps across several interface and workflow types.

N.claim: Targeted files and code selections constrain the scope of specified changes.

NE.claim: Targeted edits can coexist with locked files, making retained code directly inspectable.

E.claim: File and directory locks provide strong preservation boundaries for excluded code.

SE.claim: Existing-project planning proposes changes informed by retained code context.

S.claim: Plan Mode develops design suggestions and implementation options before a build.

SW.claim: Early planning compares functional and visual possibilities for a new app.

W.claim: Generates new multi-part websites and applications beyond one fixed template.

NW.claim: A chosen implementation plan becomes editable code and a working preview.

adjustments.reason: Restrain constrained proposals relative to explicit file targeting and locks.

name: v0
scope: v0 web app generation and latest-runtime Design Mode with sandbox tests; desktop editing, plan-dependent usage.
summary: Interfaces move between open invention and selected visual edits with reviewable code.
limitation: Design edits still generate code; a matching preview does not prove production correctness or exact screenshot reconstruction.

centerEvidence.claim: Creating and refining a new interface emphasizes invention with substantial local control.

sources.title: What is v0?
sources.finding: Generates full-stack apps and interfaces from prompts and mockups, with iteration and project planning.

sources.title: v0 Design mode
sources.finding: Selected elements accept style parameters and instructions, produce live before/after previews, and apply as reviewable code versions.

sources.title: v0 agentic features
sources.finding: Browser critique, screenshots, error fixes and sandbox terminal tests support iterative implementation.

N.claim: Selected elements, style values and code diffs give precise local control with verifiable results.

NE.claim: Selected visual changes become a new code version whose diff can be reviewed and reverted.

E.claim: Element selection and source-code diffs support structural retention, not guaranteed pixel equivalence.

SE.claim: Existing interfaces can be inspected and critiqued before revised design approaches.

S.claim: Plans, prototypes and browser critique develop alternative interface approaches.

SW.claim: Prototypes and iterative design critique develop new app directions.

W.claim: Full-stack and visual interface generation support broad composition across app structure and content.

NW.claim: A specified interface change combines generation with element selection and browser checks.

adjustments.reason: Accent selected-interface construction with local instructions and reviewable code, inside both cardinal limits.

name: Browser/computer-use agents
scope: Representative: ChatGPT Work on web/mobile for eligible paid accounts with cloud browsing enabled, reviewable files and permitted plugins. Website sign-in is limited by plan/rollout and does not enlarge this profile.
summary: A goal becomes a sequence of browser steps and a finished result you can review.
limitation: This represents ChatGPT Work, not every agent; website availability, permissions and authentication constrain actions.

centerEvidence.claim: A bounded website-to-deliverable task delegates execution while retaining human criteria and review.

sources.title: Get started with ChatGPT Work
sources.finding: Creates reviewable files from sources, uses approved tools, accepts steering and performs recurring workflows.

sources.title: ChatGPT Work browser
sources.finding: Reads, clicks and types across websites; can compare options and perform bounded actions with access controls and confirmations.

N.claim: Specified online steps have visible outcomes, while consequential actions require confirmation.

NE.claim: Selected website workflows use supplied criteria and inspectable results, without guaranteed perfect transfer.

E.claim: Files, source constraints and reviewable deliverables support evidence-bound work, short of universal exact preservation.

SE.claim: Comparing plans or listings keeps proposed options tied to retrieved facts and user criteria.

S.claim: A goal can develop into a plan and recommendations revised through follow-up guidance.

SW.claim: Drafts and recommendations supply new structure within a delegated outcome.

W.claim: Briefs, decks and other artifacts allow substantial composition across content and structure.

NW.claim: An explicit deliverable brief controls generation and revision of finished files.

name: Perplexity Computer
scope: Cloud Computer with an active subscription and available credits; authorized plugins and generated documents/apps. Portable hardware mode excluded.
summary: Research, creation and connected actions form a broad workflow around a delegated outcome.
limitation: A long workflow does not prove precise preservation; permissions, output quality and usage need inspection.

centerEvidence.claim: A research-to-artifact assignment mixes synthesis and invention with delegated delivery steps.

sources.title: What is Computer?
sources.finding: Chains cited research, analysis, document/media/code creation, connected actions and scheduled follow-up in a cloud sandbox.

N.claim: A specified research-to-delivery workflow executes across tools, though precise compliance needs review.

NE.claim: A requested comparison can become a sourced table and branded deck within one workflow.

E.claim: Cited research and connected context ground deliverables without exact preservation guarantees.

SE.claim: Competitive analysis uses retrieved evidence to develop a comparative account.

S.claim: Multi-step research and analysis support bounded proposed approaches; orchestration alone adds no design agency.

SW.claim: Research-informed artifact composition offers novel framing and organization.

W.claim: Documents, media, slides and code support substantial new compositions across output types.

NW.claim: One brief can specify a branded presentation built from conducted research.

adjustments.reason: Do not let long cross-tool execution imply exact evidence preservation.

name: Blotato
scope: Blotato paid content workspace: source remix, custom writing prompts, AI media and connected social scheduling; API access varies.
summary: Source material becomes platform-specific post variants and a controlled publishing sequence.
limitation: Style imitation and remixing do not preserve facts exactly; photo uploads are media attachments, not remix sources.

centerEvidence.claim: A source-to-post workflow delegates composition while keeping platform and publication decisions explicit.

sources.title: Blotato introduction
sources.finding: Remixes source content into social formats, creates AI media and schedules distribution.

sources.title: Make output sound like you
sources.finding: Custom prompts, examples and guidelines condition tone, structure and source-based expansion.

sources.title: Blotato FAQs
sources.finding: Drafts, supplied media, scheduled times and calendar status support controlled publication; sources and media attachments differ.

N.claim: Scheduled times, drafts and calendar states give explicit, inspectable distribution control.

NE.claim: Existing draft text and supplied media can be scheduled and reviewed as calendar entries.

E.claim: Selected sources and style examples condition output, while expansion can alter meaning.

SE.claim: A source and chosen template produce nearby post interpretations for review.

S.claim: Remixing and inspiration support content angles within social posting, not general design strategy.

SW.claim: Multiple social formats and generated media offer bounded creative alternatives.

W.claim: New captions, scripts and media extend beyond simple extractive summaries.

NW.claim: Detailed examples and guidelines direct new post composition from supplied sources.
